heading: Monday, August 10, 2026
topLine: Claude proves more than two-thirds of Riemann zeta zeros lie on the critical line. Also: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, an open-weight 30B agent model.

items.headline: Claude proves more than two-thirds of Riemann zeta zeros lie on the critical line
items.summary: Anthropic said an unreleased research version of Claude raised the proven share of zeta zeros that are simple and on the critical line from about 41.6% to 67.25%. The result does not prove the Riemann hypothesis. Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman verified it and posted a paper on arXiv, and the main results were formalized in Lean. Outside experts Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston looked over the paper. In September, Youness Lamzouri posted an independent, simpler proof of the bounds that credits Claude with finding them first.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, an open-weight 30B agent model
items.summary: Muse Glimmer is a 30B-parameter model for local agent workflows, released with open weights under Apache 2.0 and designed to run on a single consumer GPU or high-memory Mac when quantized to about 4-bit. It is the first Meta Superintelligence Labs model with open weights; Meta claims strong results for its size against Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B.
